identity.title: Are the miracles of Jesus unbelievable? Michael Shermer vs Luuk Vandeweghe
identity.dateBasis: Publisher identifies this as the NW Miracles Conference in Sequim; conference participant Sean George’s official speaking listing dates the same event March 30, 2019. Publisher’s debate episode is dated April 20, 2019.
identity.speakerIdentityBasis: Named host introductions and uninterrupted formal speeches, explicit named handoffs. Shermer explicitly affirms the question at 7:29 and in his closing, so pro is Shermer, con Vandeweghe.

acquisition.method: YouTube public Innertube Android player captions; srv3 XML normalized locally

content.coverageNote: Captions run from the opening through the final host thanks, ending about ten seconds before nominal duration. All six complete formal speeches are present; any ending remainder follows the concluding host farewell.
content.captionCaution: Automatic captions corrupt names, technical terms, some numbers and negations. No audio verification was possible; explicit restrictions bar reliance on the corrupt clauses.

participants.substantiveAdvocatesInOriginal: Two formal opponents plus substantive host prompts and audience questions in excluded informal discussion
participants.controllerExcludedMaterialReview: Controller read all 2849 canonical events, including introductory montage and entire informal discussion, to establish boundaries; truncated combined-read remainder was explicitly reread.

editorApprovedScope.userApproval: The user supplied this next video under the same invoked addition skill after instructing “Assess only the formal debates and closings.” This continuing scope is applied to this recording; no new user reply or automatic moderator exception is claimed.
editorApprovedScope.requiredReaderDisclosure: This assessment covers both formal opening statements and rebuttals (approximately 6:56–1:11:59), plus both closing statements (1:49:07–1:58:23). The entire moderated discussion and audience Q&A, including both speakers’ answers and dependent replies, and the introductory montage and surrounding host remarks are excluded at the editor’s request. Neither speaker receives credit or penalty for excluded material. These scores assess the formal rounds and closings, not the complete recording.

excludedIntervals.reason: Exclude the complete informal moderated discussion announced at events 1647–1656, all audience questions, both speakers’ answers and dependent replies, and the transition into formally announced closings. Resume only at Shermer’s closing voice after the mixed host transition; closing arguments must stand on retained evidence.

editorApprovedScope.boundaryBasis: Shermer opening events 173–670 (mixed host handoff 671–672 excluded); Vandeweghe opening 690–1141, apart from timing exchange 970–973; Shermer rebuttal 1145–1369 (mixed introduction 1144 excluded); Vandeweghe rebuttal 1377–1639 (mixed event 1376 excluded); Shermer closing 2608–2745; Vandeweghe closing 2748–2835 (mixed handoff 2747 excluded). Intervening host logistics and applause unscored. Caption intervals overlap at handoffs; select no mixed or excluded words.
editorApprovedScope.outsideWindowDisposition: Introductory host remarks and the promotional montage of Shermer before his live opening, plus host thanks after event 2835, are outside assessment and may provide no evidence or burden.
editorApprovedScope.coherenceReview: Both openings, rebuttals and closings are retained; no formal cross-examination exists. Informal discussion is excluded wholesale. Vandeweghe’s closing reference to his father’s story may be considered only as independently stated in the closing, never with details from the excluded discussion. Do not penalize either side for not answering arguments in the excluded segment.

participants.questionHandling: Whole informal discussion and Q&A excluded, including every primary answer and dependent reply. Host logistics within formal speeches unscored.

duplicateAudit.identityNote: No supplied video or Shermer–Vandeweghe pairing found in catalogue, ledger or standalone records.
